industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the tape's disagreement now the loudest in the table and the row named as the likeliest source of the tilt scorecard's negative spread. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: C now, D prior at the industry, with Hotels A, Online retail A, Physical retail B and Apparel B: the market is buying the European consumer. The reasons that set F (United States consumer surveys falling, the European consumer never read, a regime that sells discretionary spend) could not be re-tested: no consumer survey for any G10 country was in window this week. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Held because nothing on the causes side changed and a move on the tape alone against two unread legs would be a moved goalpost; the exceptions stay at sector level (Physical retail C). Counter-case: a double notch on 138 stocks against four sectors at A or B on relative strength shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists for the industry where cheap good businesses accumulate, and eight weeks of negative tilt spreads are consistent with this row being wrong. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or a second industry reading at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): big-ticket consumer purchases financed at higher rates under a low United States consumer reading; the turning note's falling side has the premium carmakers and suppliers as its widest group (seven of 25 failing the negative test, BMW and Mercedes-Benz each minus 15 points relative over 20 days), with autos not spoken to by any source. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-09 against 2026-08-07, not week on week: F now, F prior. Held at D, not F, because the evidence for a second notch is a brainstorm and because the MI Pool holds no name in this row. Counter-case: the strongest balance sheets are first to be right-sized and first to recover.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.

memo.verdict: PROGRESS to Early-Stage Assessment, low-to-moderate conviction, direction NEUTRAL. The memo explicitly overrides the Risks family's park verdict on stated grounds, and concedes one of the two park conditions remains open. Condition for progression: Early-Stage Assessment must resolve the Luce electric-vehicle margin structure and test whether personalisation above 20% is a structural baseline or a cyclical peak. Escalation clause carried in the memo: if the Luce margin work cannot be completed from available sources, the recommendation reverts to the Risks family's park verdict rather than proceeding on an unresolved gate. Direction is stated as neutral, not bullish, because business quality is not in question and price is.
case: The argument runs in four steps.

First, the business quality is not in dispute anywhere in the source pack. FY25 pre-tax return on capital employed of 53.5% sits against Porsche at 6.9% and the closest peer-set comparator, Knorr-Bremse, at approximately 22.0%; Fincantieri runs sub-4% historical EBIT margins. Ferrari generates roughly EUR 155,000 of operating profit per car sold. Working capital is structurally negative. Volume resilience is the hardest evidence in the pack: shipments fell only 3.00% during the 2008 global financial crisis, against Bentley down 54.00%, Aston Martin down 43.00% and Lamborghini down 41.00%.

Second, competitive position is exceptional and graded A. Porsche AG recorded a 1.1% operating return on sales in 2025, with operating result falling from EUR 5.6bn in 2024 to EUR 0.4bn in 2025. Aston Martin posted a negative adjusted operating profit of GBP 189.2m in 2025. Lamborghini achieved a 27.00% operating margin in 2024 but average revenue per unit of EUR 289.60k lagged Ferrari's EUR 416.50k by 43.80%. In the collectible segment Ferrari stands completely alone. No peer in the named set graded A on Element E11, so this is a deliberate outlier call anchored on those peer profit figures.
counter_case: The Risks family's stage-progression verdict is park, quoted in the memo in its own words: "we recommend pausing the investment idea until hybrid residuals stabilize and the Luce EV margin structure is clear", and separately, "a cautious hold-and-watch stance is recommended rather than immediate progression". The memo does not soften this and carries it into the grades.

The load-bearing counter is the false-friend finding, graded D at Element E8 RA8 and named the single most important finding in the memo. The Risks family's competing-hypotheses matrix, run across fifteen indicators, makes the FALSE FRIEND profile the winner with only two minor structural inconsistencies, against five hard inconsistencies for the bull profile and eight for the bear profile. The masked signal is the order book: coverage extending through 2027 remains highly supportive yet hides underlying dealer allocation coercion. The mechanism is that dealers reportedly force buyers to purchase the Luce electric vehicle to remain eligible for limited-edition V12s, described as the most dangerous and least monitored execution failure mode. Three further false friends are carried: elevated personalisation above 20% is argued to increase future vehicle resale depreciation, with management having formally warned about personalisation depreciation; stabilising hybrid resale values may hide structural dealer trade-in manipulation, since dealers artificially support trade-in values to close new vehicle sales; and working capital tailwinds are expected to normalise as customer down payments unwind, with Q2 2026 already showing a EUR 103m working capital outflow. The finding is independently corroborated in a second family: the leadership-foundations family separately records expert calls revealing emerging dealer inventory build-ups for hybrid models, contrasting official zero-inventory guidance.
triggers: Gating question for Early-Stage Assessment: resolve the Luce electric-vehicle margin structure and the e-building amortisation bridge before any valuation modelling.

Second open question: whether personalisation above 20% is a structural baseline or a cyclical peak, named by the earnings-review family as the primary risk to the investment thesis. Stated invalidation trigger: personalisation normalising below 18% of cars and spare parts revenues with full-year EBIT margins at or below 29.5% without further upward revision.
Third open question: whether the order book through 2027 is genuine demand or a false friend. The decisive test is separating organic Luce order velocity from allocation-linked orders.

Named formal triggers carried from the Risks family: hybrid residual values declining 10% requires the pre-mortem to be re-run immediately; customer order cancellation rates rising past 10% converts the false-friend thesis into outright failure, against a standard reported cancellation rate of 10%; Luce shipments falling below 1,000 units annually requires impairment testing of e-building assets; producing over 15,000 units annually is a formal trigger to reassess brand exclusivity.

Luce secondary-market trigger from the earnings-review family: initial secondary market transactions showing depreciation exceeding 20% below MSRP within twelve months of delivery would replicate the Porsche Taycan value-destruction pattern.
Valuation re-open trigger: a multiple reset toward the EUR 240 to EUR 262 sell-side bear range, at which point the paradigm-fit objection at Element E5 RA4 would resolve in the stock's favour.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
